dedupe_keys.name: geul catchment nl be de nature based solutions versus building level flood measures with the coupled geb model bril and co authors wrr 2026

description: This case study compares nature-based solutions with building-level flood measures in the Geul catchment, shared by the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany and heavily flooded in July 2021. Veerle Bril, Jens de Bruijn, Hans de Moel, Tarun Sadana, Tim Busker, Wouter Botzen and Jeroen Aerts of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Deltares and IIASA published it in Water Resources Research in 2026. They extend the open source GEB model by coupling it to a hydrodynamic and a flood risk model, so that reforestation, natural grassland, retention ponds, dry-proofing and wet-proofing are assessed catchment-wide for flood extent, depth, damage and risk. Reforestation and grassland of 10 km2 each reduce extent by 12% and damage by up to 38%, deeper ponds help little, and dry-proofing cuts damage by up to 95% against about 55% for wet-proofing. Coverage is one catchment. Format and access: an open access article; the publisher page asks for a browser check, so the abstract was read through OpenAlex. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: results depend on the scenarios and on one extreme event. It informs adaptation planning that mixes green-blue and building measures. Related catalogue records are the GEB model and the Mangrove hybrid defence study.
